turns.speaker: Woman
turns.text: All twelve samples need a single run. The customer’s report needs the chamber log and a post-run inspection that only my team can sign.

turns.speaker: Man
turns.text: On Wednesday, only the small chamber is free. It holds eight. The large chamber holds sixteen and is free Friday morning or afternoon. I can hold a slot before approval.

turns.speaker: Woman
turns.text: Our technician can load only after noon. Only our engineer can sign the plan, and she works remotely.

turns.speaker: Man
turns.text: The desk checks signed plans before admitting samples. There’s no signal beyond it. The chamber sends its log to your manager when it stops.

questions.prompt: Which booking would let the team run the entire batch?
options: Book the small chamber on Wednesday and divide the batch.
Book the large chamber on Friday morning and load it as booked.
Book the large chamber on Friday afternoon and keep the batch together.
Book the large chamber on Wednesday and load it after noon.

questions.prompt: How should the woman arrange approval and entry?
options: Hold a slot, bring the samples inside, then call the engineer.
Hold a slot, get the engineer’s signature while still outside, and show it at the desk before taking in the samples.
Hold a slot and ask the desk to sign the plan before the samples enter.
Have the engineer sign remotely, take the samples inside, and show the plan on the way out.

questions.prompt: If the run ends on a day when no one on her team is working, what can happen that day?
options: The manager can get the chamber log, but the customer’s report must wait.
The customer can get the report once the chamber sends its log.
The manager cannot receive anything until the team signs the inspection.
The chamber sends the log directly to the customer while the manager waits for the inspection.
